text:
Leo H: Follow-up from the multi-region RFC meeting. Need a short, implementable plan for billing attribution + auditability when active/active failover kicks in. Keep it runnable.

Anya V: Two distinct asks: (1) Accurate infra-cost attribution, (2) provable residency audit trail. They overlap but solve different stakeholder needs (Finance vs Legal/Product).

Marcus P: Current reality: costs get tagged by runner_region at runtime. That's simple but flips invoices when traffic moves. Finance dislikes surprise flips.

Leo H: Proposal: introduce a per-tenant billing_policy with three options: `home`, `served`, `hybrid`. Default = `home` for enterprise/residency tenants, `served` for self-serve.

Anya V: Hybrid rule idea: charge cold-start overheads to served for the first T seconds (default 60s) or first N tokens, then bill steady-state to home. Makes sense for warmup-heavy workloads.

Marcus P: Tech surface: we need to propagate (and sign) these fields: `X-RWI-Home`, `X-RWI-Served`, `X-RWI-Policy`, `X-RWI-Ts` and a signature header `X-RWI-Sig`. Edge signs, downstream validates.

Leo H: Agree on signing. Threat model: untrusted clients or rogue internal proxies could spoof headers. HMAC with KMS keys solves it. Add signature of tenant_id|home|served|ts. Include sig version.

Anya V: Audit requirement: collectors must persist home+served+policy+sig into request-level logs and traces. For async tasks, encode the same metadata into task payloads.

Marcus P: Reconciliation job: daily batch that consumes cost_by_region and enriched logs, allocates cost per tenant per policy. Output table: tenant_id, billing_day, billed_region, cost_cents, reason_flags (failover,cold_start,manual_override).

OpsBot: NOTE: manual failovers must emit an `ops:override` event and set `X-RWI-Override: user:<name>` on requests initiated during the override. This will be recorded in logs.

billing-bot: FYI finance wants a reconciliation endpoint to pull per-tenant deltas for disputed invoices. Add to RFC.

Leo H: Edge cases noted: many-to-one fanout (subcalls across regions), queued workers executing elsewhere, and multi-model fanout with differing hardware costs. Reconciliation must accept joinable child records and attribute proportionally by resource usage (tokens/latency).

Anya V: Minimal action items for RFC follow-up: 1) header names + sig spec + example, 2) collectors schema change, 3) recon job algorithm + SQL examples, 4) console UI tweaks (events timeline + billing policy toggle), 5) retention + export options for residency customers, 6) tests (failover simulation + cold-start billing).

Marcus P: Implementation rough sizing: edge signing filter (1w), collector ingest + schema (1w), recon job (2w), console + docs (1w). Parallel teams.

Leo H: Owners: Marcus -> edge prototype + PR, Anya -> recon algorithm and console mock, Finance (cc @billing-bot) -> validation endpoints, Legal -> retention terms.

Anya V: Quick header example for the RFC:
```
X-RWI-Home: eu-1
X-RWI-Served: us-3
X-RWI-Policy: hybrid
X-RWI-Ts: 2026-03-23T09:12:04Z
X-RWI-Sig: v1:base64hmac
```

Marcus P: I'll include HMAC pseudo-code and a KMS rotation note in the PR. Use SHA256 HMAC and include ttl check on Ts. Reject if ts > 2 min skew.

Leo H: Also require a flag in tenant profile for `residency_required` which forces `home` policy and limits overrides. Product must add an approval flow for any ops override when that flag is set.

Anya V: Good. I'll add that to the compliance checklist: residency flag, export retention (12/36/retainer options), redaction rules for PII, and audit report generation.

billing-bot: Created ticket #5099: "multi-region billing-policy + signed routing headers" assigned to Marcus P.

Leo H: Thanks. I'll open the RFC follow-up with this checklist and assign owners. Ping here if you need me to expand the recon SQL example.
